metadata.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
metadata.description: We give a deterministic reduction for complete sparse univariate polynomial factorization over explicitly represented finite fields. The bit cost is polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and the total degree of the distinct densely returned factors, with arbitrary binary multiplicities. A sparse numerator and dense denominator are maintained through characteristic-p descent; denominator degree grows by at most the original radical degree per step. Classical Pade reconstruction, logarithmic derivatives, residue multiplicity methods and Cartier sections are attributed to their original sources. The paper also details inherited dense factorization and prescribed-degree irreducible construction consequences of OpenAI family142 through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. The upstream prime-field theorem requires family029 general cyclotomic Hecke zero-freeness. No randomness, GRH or integer-factorization oracle is introduced. Construction degree and optional fixed-root degree are numeric dense parameters; no general binary-degree construction/root bound or practical efficiency is claimed. The sparse theorem is not a sparse-output GCD or arbitrary-circuit theorem. Alec Kriebel is the sole author. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing; automated adversarial audits are not human peer review. No assertion of first priority or upstream breakthrough ownership is made. The verification archive includes proofs, exact source references, independent audits and feasible reference reductions. Its bounded exhaustive prime oracle is toy-only; no full-follow-on formal verification or execution of the enormous prime-field branch is claimed.
